categories.name: Feedback & System Status
categories.blurb: Does every action produce a visible, timely response?

categories.name: Error Prevention & Recovery
categories.principle: Nielsen #5 & #9 — Error prevention; help users recover
categories.blurb: Do things break, and can users recover when they do?

categories.name: Interaction Efficiency
categories.blurb: Are targets easy to hit and does the UI respond in < 400 ms?

categories.name: Cognitive Load
categories.blurb: Is the number of choices and the amount of content manageable?

categories.name: Frustration Signals
categories.blurb: What real interaction behaviour says about confusion.

categories.name: Forms & Input
categories.blurb: Can users complete inputs without friction?

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.principle: WCAG 2.2 AA — Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust
categories.blurb: Can everyone perceive and operate the interface?

categories.name: Consistency & Standards
categories.blurb: Do things that look the same behave the same, and follow conventions?

categories.name: Performance
categories.blurb: Does it load fast and stay visually stable?

categories.name: Design System Compliance
categories.blurb: Does the UI use the design system’s colours, type, spacing and components?

findings.title: Font “Arial” is not part of Echo UI
findings.detail: Used 3× across 1 page. Closest token: Urbanist.
findings.fix: Use the nearest token (Urbanist) instead of a one-off value.

findings.principle: Nielsen #1 — Visibility of system status
findings.title: Dead click on “Search flights”
findings.detail: 1 click produced no visible change (no DOM update, no navigation) within 1 s. The element is interactive, so feedback is missing or delayed.
findings.fix: Provide immediate visual feedback (active state, spinner, toast) for every action.
